punchline: Gawande says to ask a seriously ill patient what a good day looks like before asking which treatment they want.
thirty_sec: Surgeon Atul Gawande was never taught how to talk with a dying patient. In a study of advanced lung cancer, patients who received early palliative care talked about their fears and goals. They chose less aggressive care, reported better quality of life, and lived a few months longer on average. His call: let the patient set the measure for the time that remains.
